key_insight: IRMAE-WD’s latent singular-value drop marks the effective dimension of its trained representation, not necessarily the intrinsic degrees of freedom of turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Compact representations of wall turbulence should be selected for a required reconstruction accuracy or resolved scale, rather than a single dimension estimate.
method: Apply IRMAE-WD with a 3D convolutional autoencoder to minimal-channel velocity fields at Reτ = 110.
Vary the number of linear layers and truncate latent coordinates at the singular-value drop.
Use transfer learning to compare coordinate requirements against POD by reconstruction accuracy and reproduced scale.
evidence_signal: Truncation at the drop reduced reconstruction rate by at most 0.01 percentage points; with transfer learning, IRMAE-WD needed fewer coordinates than POD up to about 97% reconstruction, while POD was more compact above that level.
watch_item: The drop shifts toward fewer dimensions as linear layers are added, so it should not be treated as an architecture-independent measure of intrinsic flow dimension.
paper_title: Effective-dimension estimation of a minimal turbulent channel flow via IRMAE-WD
